content.text: Column already exists from 20240521090000, so the new migration is data-only. Now the runner it needs to plug into.
Writing the hand-authored SQL migration. Data-only, idempotent (guarded on "dueDate" IS NULL), no DDL.

input.content:
-- Backfill due dates for tasks created before "dueDate" existed.
-- Column comes from 20240521090000_add_task_due_date; no DDL in this migration.
-- Idempotent: only rows where "dueDate" IS NULL are touched.

UPDATE "Task"
SET "dueDate" = "createdAt" + INTERVAL '7 days'
WHERE "dueDate" IS NULL
  AND "status" IN ('OPEN', 'IN_PROGRESS');

-- Completed tasks inherit their completion timestamp.
UPDATE "Task"
SET "dueDate" = "completedAt"
WHERE "dueDate" IS NULL
  AND "status" = 'DONE'
  AND "completedAt" IS NOT NULL;

content.text:
Done. Two files changed:

- `prisma/migrations/20240614093000_backfill_task_due_dates/migration.sql` — hand-written, data-only: open/in-progress tasks get `createdAt + INTERVAL '7 days'`, done tasks get `completedAt`. Both statements guard on `"dueDate" IS NULL`, so re-running is a no-op. No DDL; the column already exists from 20240521090000.
- `scripts/backfill.ts` — registered the new migration, and `runMigration` now splits the file into statements and applies them in a single transaction.

First test run failed 2/10 on my new `splitSql` (naive `';'` split kept the comment header and a trailing empty chunk). Fixed it to strip line comments and drop empty statements; second run is 10/10 passing.

`git diff --stat` confirms only those two files changed — `prisma/schema.prisma` is untouched. I did not execute `npm run migrate` against a database, so the SQL is verified by the suite but has not been applied to any live data.
